name: Ethical Purchasing Group - SIA Project 22 23
description:
The system supports the management of an Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS), known in Italian as a Gruppo di Acquisto Solidale (GAS), associated with a km-zero fruit and vegetable store. The purpose of the system is to connect groups of customers with local farmers and store employees, supporting a conscious purchasing process based on knowledge of product origin, quality, characteristics, availability, and price.

The operating cycle of the purchasing group is organized on a weekly basis. Farmers provide estimates of the products they can supply between Friday at noon and Saturday morning. For each available product, farmers specify the product type, quantity, price, and optionally additional crop characteristics such as size, quality, or ripeness.

The information system maintains a catalogue of products containing descriptions, photographs, the unit of measurement used for sale, and the minimum and maximum quantities that can be ordered. Each availability entered by a farmer refers to one of the products contained in the catalogue.

Customers can browse the offers provided by the different farmers and place orders by selecting products and specifying the desired quantities. Customers are representatives of purchasing groups, such as families or groups of people, and only the registered representative of each group can submit an order.

Orders can be entered directly by customers through the web system or by store employees on behalf of customers. Before an order can be confirmed, the system checks that the quantities selected respect the minimum order constraints defined for each product. If the minimum quantities are not met, the customer must modify the order. After completion, the system sends an order summary to the customer by email.

Customer orders initially remain in an entered state until farmers confirm the actual quantities available by Monday morning. If the available quantities are sufficient to satisfy all orders, the orders are confirmed. When the available quantity of a product is insufficient, the system applies precedence rules based on customer priority and removes unavailable quantities from lower-priority orders.

Orders modified because of limited product availability are placed in a modified state and must be reviewed and explicitly accepted by customers. If every product in an order becomes unavailable, the order is cancelled.

After farmers confirm product availability, the system automatically performs payment for the quantities actually included in the order. Payments are made through a personal virtual wallet associated with each customer. Customers can recharge their wallet through the store at any time.

If a customer's wallet balance is insufficient immediately after order placement, the customer receives an email warning, but the order remains valid. If the balance is insufficient when the automatic payment is executed, the customer receives an SMS and has until Monday evening to recharge the wallet. If the required balance is still unavailable at that time, the order is cancelled.

Once payment has been successfully completed, customers can reserve a time slot for collecting their products from the store. Store employees can view the pickup schedule at the beginning of their shifts and prepare the packages corresponding to customer orders. When a customer arrives, the employee confirms the collection of the order.

If a customer fails to collect the order at the scheduled time, the system sends an SMS reminder. If the order has not been collected by Friday, the order is marked as forfeited and the customer's fair-play score is updated.

Farmers deliver their products to the store by Tuesday evening. Store employees confirm the receipt of the delivered quantities. If the goods have not arrived by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, the system sends an SMS reminder. If the goods have still not been delivered by 8 p.m., the related customer orders are updated, the missing amount is credited back to the affected customers with an additional 20 percent bonus, and the customers are informed of the delivery problem.

The system maintains a fair-play score for each customer. The score represents the reliability of the customer with respect to previous orders and is used as a precedence criterion when product availability is insufficient. The score is computed from the number of completed orders, reminders received, forfeited pickups, and modified orders. Customers with higher fair-play scores are given precedence over customers with lower scores when limited quantities must be allocated among competing orders.

highLevelGoals: Enable customers to make informed purchasing decisions by providing detailed information about product origin, quality, and availability.
Facilitate the submission, modification, and confirmation of customer orders while respecting minimum quantity constraints and prioritizing high-fair-play-score customers during shortages.
Allow customers to securely manage virtual wallets, receive timely payment notifications, and handle insufficient balances with grace periods and automatic cancellations if necessary.
Provide customers with time slots for product collection, notify them of missed pickups, and enforce forfeit policies to maintain system reliability.
Allow farmers to submit product availability estimates and enable the system to dynamically adjust order fulfillment based on real-time availability and precedence rules.
Use a fair-play score system to prioritize customers during product shortages, ensuring equitable treatment based on historical reliability.
Allow store employees to manage orders, coordinate pickups, handle payments, and manage delivery confirmations to ensure smooth daily operations.
Alert farmers and customers of delivery delays, automatically credit back missing amounts with bonus, and maintain transparency about delivery status.
Ensure that all transactions, payments, and pickups are accurately recorded and enforced, with mechanisms to penalize or reward customer behavior based on reliability.
Enable only registered representatives of purchasing groups to submit orders, ensuring accountability and group-based purchasing integrity.

baselineCritiques.actors: The actors defined are mostly appropriate, but there is redundancy between "Customer" and "Purchasing Group Representative." A customer is already described as a representative of a purchasing group, so having both roles separately is unnecessary. Additionally, while the description covers all key entities involved in the system (customers, store employees, farmers), it could be more precise to distinguish between different types of customers (e.g., individual customers vs. representatives) if needed for clarity. However, no critical omissions or contradictions are present.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are comprehensive and well-aligned with the system's description. They cover all functional aspects of the Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS) management, including product sourcing, order management, payment processing, pickup scheduling, inventory tracking, fair allocation, store operations, delivery management, system integrity, and group-based purchasing. No contradictions or omissions are detected.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are generally well-aligned with the high-level goals and the system description. However, there are a few minor issues that could be addressed for better completeness and accuracy: 1. Missing Low-Level Goal for Farmer's Initial Availability Submission: - The high-level goal "[Farmer] Maintain accurate inventory and availability tracking" implies that farmers should initially submit their product availability estimates (between Friday noon and Saturday morning). While this is partially covered under "Submit product availability estimate," it lacks specificity about the timing or process constraints (e.g., deadline for submission). 2. Overlap in Low-Level Goals: - Some low-level goals, such as those related to notifications (e.g., "Notify customer of order changes due to insufficient availability"), are duplicated across branches (e.g., also under "[Customer] Optimize product pickup scheduling and collection"). This redundancy could be streamlined. 3. Missing Clarity on API Endpoints: - Several low-level goals mention API interactions (e.g., "via API" or "via dedicated API endpoint") without specifying whether these are RESTful, GraphQL, or other types of APIs. While this is a technical detail, it could be clarified for completeness. 4. Inconsistency in Payment Handling: - The high-level goal "[Customer] Enable seamless payment and wallet management" includes support for partial payments, but the low-level goal "Support partial payments for orders" seems out of scope given the system description (payments are automatic upon confirmation). This could be removed or clarified. 5. Missing Low-Level Goal for Store Employee's Order Validation: - The high-level goal "[Store Employee] Enable efficient store operations and order fulfillment" does not explicitly cover the employee's role in validating orders before confirmation (e.g., checking for errors or completeness). 6. Fair-Play Score Calculation: - While the fair-play score is mentioned, there is no low-level goal specifying how it is calculated (e.g., weightings for completed orders, reminders, etc.). This could be added for clarity. 7. Missing Low-Level Goal for Customer's Order Cancellation Due to Late Delivery: - The high-level goal "[Farmer] Provide timely delivery and customer notification" includes automatic cancellation of orders if deliveries are late, but this is not explicitly covered in the low-level goals under "[Customer] Optimize product pickup scheduling and collection." 8. Missing Low-Level Goal for Farmer's Delivery Confirmation: - The high-level goal "[Farmer] Provide timely delivery and customer notification" implies that farmers should confirm receipt of delivered products, but this is not explicitly covered in the low-level goals. 9. Inconsistency in Order State Management: - The system description mentions orders being placed in "entered," "modified," or "cancelled" states, but these transitions are not clearly reflected in the low-level goals (e.g., no explicit goal for transitioning from "entered" to "confirmed"). 10. Missing Low-Level Goal for Customer's Order Summary Email: - The system description mentions sending an order summary email after submission, but this is not covered in the low-level goals. ### Suggested Improvements: - Add a low-level goal for farmers to submit initial product availability estimates by Saturday morning. - Remove or clarify the "Support partial payments for orders" goal if it is out of scope. - Specify API types (e.g., RESTful) where mentioned. - Add clarity on fair-play score calculation and order state transitions. - Include low-level goals for store employees to validate orders and confirm delivery receipt by farmers. - Add a low-level goal for sending order summary emails post-submission.

hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to browse farmer offers, compare products, place orders with minimum quantity constraints, modify orders due to availability issues using precedence and fair-play rules, review and accept modified orders, and cancel orders when all products are unavailable with notification.
hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.rationale: llg_001 enables viewing product origin details including certifications and availability; llg_002 enables browsing and comparing farmer offers by price, quantity, and characteristics; llg_003 enables placing orders with minimum quantity constraints; llg_004 enables modifying orders due to availability constraints using precedence rules and fair-play score; llg_005 enables reviewing and accepting modified orders; llg_006 enables automatic cancellation of orders when all products are unavailable with customer notification.

hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to submit, modify, confirm, and receive notifications for order changes due to insufficient availability, while enforcing minimum quantity requirements.
hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to submit orders with minimum quantity constraints; llg_002 allows modification of existing orders (including quantity or item changes); llg_003 triggers confirmation and system validation; llg_004 introduces a distinct capability: notifying customers of changes due to insufficient availability and allowing API-based acceptance/rejection — which is materially different from the other goals and must be explicitly included to expose the scope mismatch.

hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to monitor wallet balances, receive payment notifications, manage insufficient funds with grace periods, recharge wallets via in-store terminals or online transfers, and process partial payments for orders.
hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to check wallet balance and payment status, which supports awareness of fund availability. llg_002 enables real-time payment notifications, ensuring transparency during transactions. llg_003 introduces a grace period for insufficient balance, allowing customers to avoid immediate order cancellation. llg_004 enables wallet recharging via in-store terminals, supporting physical access to payment methods. llg_005 enables wallet recharging via online transfer, supporting digital access to payment methods. llg_006 enables partial payments for orders, allowing flexible payment structuring. Together, these capabilities form a complete wallet and payment lifecycle system with no hidden or inferred functionality.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Check wallet balance and payment status
Handle insufficient balance with grace period

hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to schedule, be notified about, and handle consequences of product pickup appointments at physical stores.
hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to select a pickup time slot based on store availability; llg_002 ensures customers receive a reminder notification before pickup to confirm attendance; llg_003 ensures customers are notified if they miss pickup and are informed of forfeit policy consequences — together, these cover the full lifecycle of a pickup appointment including scheduling, pre-event notification, and post-missed-event consequence handling.

hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable farmers to submit, update, and confirm product availability estimates for dynamic allocation and order fulfillment, with real-time updates and a Monday-morning confirmation deadline.
hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.rationale: llg_001 enables initial submission of product availability estimates for dynamic allocation; llg_002 adds real-time update capability via API to reflect stock or delivery changes; llg_003 introduces a mandatory Monday-morning confirmation of final quantities available for order, which is a distinct lifecycle phase and deadline not covered by the other goals.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Confirm final product quantities available for order

hlg_5c82e14395e9d14b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a dynamic customer prioritization system during shortages that calculates, updates, and displays a fair-play score based on order behavior, enabling automated prioritization of customer orders and transparent score visibility.
hlg_5c82e14395e9d14b_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to automatically prioritize customer orders during shortages using a fair-play score. llg_002 adds the capability for customers to view their fair-play score to understand their priority level. llg_003 adds the capability to calculate and update the fair-play score dynamically via API based on completed orders, reminders, or penalties. Together, these form a complete system: score calculation, score visibility, and automated prioritization during shortages — with no inferred or omitted functionality.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Prioritize customer based on fair-play score

hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable store employees to manage end-to-end order fulfillment, including coordination of product pickup, processing customer payments, and confirming delivery status via system updates.
hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.rationale: llg_001 enables store employees to view and manage pending orders for fulfillment; llg_002 adds the capability to coordinate pickup logistics including time and location; llg_003 introduces payment processing and wallet balance updates via system API; llg_004 adds the capability to confirm delivery status and update system records. Together, these cover the full lifecycle of order fulfillment from initiation to delivery confirmation, with explicit handling of pickup logistics and payment integration.

hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Notify stakeholders of delivery delays, automatically credit back missing amounts with 20% bonus, cancel late orders, and provide estimated resolution times via API.
hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.rationale: llg_001 adds notification to farmers and automatic 20% bonus credit on delays; llg_002 adds notification to customers and estimated resolution time; llg_003 adds automatic 20% bonus credit for missing amounts; llg_004 adds order cancellation and 20% bonus credit for late deliveries — all via API. These capabilities are materially distinct and must be preserved, including the outlier llg_004 which introduces order cancellation as a distinct action not covered by the others.

hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to browse farmer offers, compare products, place orders with minimum quantity constraints, modify orders due to availability issues using precedence and fair-play rules, review and accept modified orders, and cancel orders when all products are unavailable with notification.
hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.rationale: llg_001 enables viewing product origin details including certifications and availability; llg_002 enables browsing and comparing farmer offers by price, quantity, and characteristics; llg_003 enables placing orders with minimum quantity constraints; llg_004 enables modifying orders due to availability constraints using precedence rules and fair-play score; llg_005 enables reviewing and accepting modified orders; llg_006 enables automatic cancellation of orders when all products are unavailable with customer notification.

Modify order due to availability constraints
Cancel order due to complete unavailability

hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to submit, modify, confirm, and receive notifications for order changes due to insufficient availability, while enforcing minimum quantity requirements.
hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to submit orders with minimum quantity constraints; llg_002 allows modification of existing orders (including quantity or item changes); llg_003 triggers confirmation and system validation; llg_004 introduces a distinct capability: notifying customers of changes due to insufficient availability and allowing API-based acceptance/rejection — which is materially different from the other goals and must be explicitly included to expose the scope mismatch.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Submit an order with minimum quantity
Notify customer of order changes due to insufficient availability

hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to monitor wallet balances, receive payment notifications, manage insufficient funds with grace periods, recharge wallets via in-store terminals or online transfers, and process partial payments for orders.
hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to check wallet balance and payment status, which supports awareness of fund availability. llg_002 enables real-time payment notifications, ensuring transparency during transactions. llg_003 introduces a grace period for insufficient balance, allowing customers to avoid immediate order cancellation. llg_004 enables wallet recharging via in-store terminals, supporting physical access to payment methods. llg_005 enables wallet recharging via online transfer, supporting digital access to payment methods. llg_006 enables partial payments for orders, allowing flexible payment structuring. Together, these capabilities form a complete wallet and payment lifecycle system with no hidden or inferred functionality.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Check wallet balance and payment status
Handle insufficient balance with grace period

hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to schedule, be notified about, and handle consequences of product pickup appointments at physical stores.
hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to select a pickup time slot based on store availability; llg_002 ensures customers receive a reminder notification before pickup to confirm attendance; llg_003 ensures customers are notified if they miss pickup and are informed of forfeit policy consequences — together, these cover the full lifecycle of a pickup appointment including scheduling, pre-event notification, and post-missed-event consequence handling.

hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable farmers to submit, update, and confirm product availability estimates for dynamic allocation and order fulfillment, with real-time updates and a Monday-morning confirmation deadline.
hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.rationale: llg_001 enables initial submission of product availability estimates for dynamic allocation; llg_002 adds real-time update capability via API to reflect stock or delivery changes; llg_003 introduces a mandatory Monday-morning confirmation of final quantities available for order, which is a distinct lifecycle phase and deadline not covered by the other goals.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Confirm final product quantities available for order

hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable store employees to manage end-to-end order fulfillment, including coordination of product pickup, processing customer payments, and confirming delivery status via system updates.
hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.rationale: llg_001 enables store employees to view and manage pending orders for fulfillment; llg_002 adds the capability to coordinate pickup logistics including time and location; llg_003 introduces payment processing and wallet balance updates via system API; llg_004 adds the capability to confirm delivery status and update system records. Together, these cover the full lifecycle of order fulfillment from initiation to delivery confirmation, with explicit handling of pickup logistics and payment integration.

hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Notify stakeholders of delivery delays, automatically credit back missing amounts with 20% bonus, cancel late orders, and provide estimated resolution times via API.
hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.rationale: llg_001 adds notification to farmers and automatic 20% bonus credit on delays; llg_002 adds notification to customers and estimated resolution time; llg_003 adds automatic 20% bonus credit for missing amounts; llg_004 adds order cancellation and 20% bonus credit for late deliveries — all via API. These capabilities are materially distinct and must be preserved, including the outlier llg_004 which introduces order cancellation as a distinct action not covered by the others.

hlg_2cf58a471a47b2bf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Record and enforce transactional obligations including payment and pickup forfeit policies via API-driven enforcement mechanisms.
hlg_2cf58a471a47b2bf_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to record transaction details and enforce payment rules via API. llg_002 adds the capability to enforce a pickup forfeit policy, deducting from wallet or marking as forfeited via API. hlg_8cc6881ea295c041_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable authorized group representatives to submit purchase orders while ensuring their identity is verified before submission.

hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to browse farmer offers, compare products, place orders with minimum quantity constraints, modify orders due to availability issues using precedence and fair-play rules, review and accept modified orders, and cancel orders when all products are unavailable with notification.
hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.rationale: llg_001 enables viewing product origin details including certifications and availability; llg_002 enables browsing and comparing farmer offers by price, quantity, and characteristics; llg_003 enables placing orders with minimum quantity constraints; llg_004 enables modifying orders due to availability constraints using precedence rules and fair-play score; llg_005 enables reviewing and accepting modified orders; llg_006 enables automatic cancellation of orders when all products are unavailable with customer notification.

hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a customer-facing order management system with wallet-based payment enforcement, fair-play scoring for order behavior, store-level fulfillment confirmation, and automated compensation for delivery failures, including SMS notifications and bonus credits.
hlg_91b57471207e9b44_001.rationale: llg_001 enables order submission with minimum quantity constraints; llg_002 allows pre-confirmation modifications; llg_003 triggers validation and allocation upon confirmation; llg_004 handles availability-driven order changes via API; llg_005 checks wallet balance at submission; llg_006 sends SMS reminders for wallet recharge before payment; llg_007 auto-cancels orders if wallet remains insufficient after Monday evening; llg_008 adjusts fair-play score for missed pickups; llg_009 adjusts fair-play score for availability-driven modifications; llg_010 confirms order collection by store employee; llg_011 confirms farmer delivery to update inventory; llg_012 sends SMS reminders if delivery is delayed past 4 p.m. Tuesday; llg_013 credits back missing amounts with 20% bonus if delivery is delayed past 8 p.m. Tuesday. Together, these LLGs define a system that manages customer orders from submission to fulfillment, enforces wallet-based payment with reminders and cancellations, tracks fair-play scores for behavioral consequences, and handles delivery failures with notifications and compensation.

hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to monitor, manage, and resolve wallet balance issues for order transactions through real-time notifications, grace periods, multiple recharge methods, and automated order cancellation if insufficient funds persist.
hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to check wallet balance and payment status, establishing visibility into funds. llg_002 provides real-time payment notifications to inform customers of transaction status. llg_003 introduces a grace period for insufficient balance, allowing customers time to top up before cancellation. llg_004 and llg_005 provide two distinct recharge methods (in-store terminal and online transfer) to replenish funds. llg_006 triggers an email warning at order placement if funds are insufficient, ensuring early alert. llg_007 triggers an SMS reminder before Monday evening to prompt timely action. llg_008 automatically cancels orders if funds remain insufficient after Monday evening, enforcing financial accountability. Together, these LLGs form a complete lifecycle for managing wallet funds during order transactions, including proactive alerts, multiple recharge options, and automated cancellation as a last resort.

hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to schedule, be notified about, and handle consequences of product pickup appointments at physical stores.
hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to select a pickup time slot based on store availability; llg_002 ensures customers receive a reminder notification before pickup to confirm attendance; llg_003 ensures customers are notified if they miss pickup and are informed of forfeit policy consequences — together, these cover the full lifecycle of a pickup appointment including scheduling, pre-event notification, and post-missed-event consequence handling.

hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable farmers to submit, update, and confirm product availability estimates for dynamic allocation and order fulfillment, with real-time updates and a Monday-morning confirmation deadline.
hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.rationale: llg_001 enables initial submission of product availability estimates for dynamic allocation; llg_002 adds real-time update capability via API to reflect stock or delivery changes; llg_003 introduces a mandatory Monday-morning confirmation of final quantities available for order, which is a distinct lifecycle phase and deadline not covered by the other goals.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Confirm final product quantities available for order

hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable store employees to manage end-to-end order fulfillment, including coordination of product pickup, processing customer payments, and confirming delivery status via system updates.
hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.rationale: llg_001 enables store employees to view and manage pending orders for fulfillment; llg_002 adds the capability to coordinate pickup logistics including time and location; llg_003 introduces payment processing and wallet balance updates via system API; llg_004 adds the capability to confirm delivery status and update system records. Together, these cover the full lifecycle of order fulfillment from initiation to delivery confirmation, with explicit handling of pickup logistics and payment integration.

hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Notify stakeholders of delivery delays, automatically credit back missing amounts with 20% bonus, cancel late orders, and provide estimated resolution times via API.
hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.rationale: llg_001 adds notification to farmers and automatic 20% bonus credit on delays; llg_002 adds notification to customers and estimated resolution time; llg_003 adds automatic 20% bonus credit for missing amounts; llg_004 adds order cancellation and 20% bonus credit for late deliveries — all via API. These capabilities are materially distinct and must be preserved, including the outlier llg_004 which introduces order cancellation as a distinct action not covered by the others.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Automatically credit back missing amount with bonus
Cancel orders and credit wallets with 20% bonus if deliveries are late

hlg_2cf58a471a47b2bf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Record and enforce transactional obligations including payment and pickup forfeit policies via API-driven enforcement mechanisms.
hlg_2cf58a471a47b2bf_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to record transaction details and enforce payment rules via API. llg_002 adds the capability to enforce a pickup forfeit policy, deducting from wallet or marking as forfeited via API. Together, they define a system that enforces financial obligations tied to transactional events — specifically payments and pickup-related forfeits — with API-driven enforcement as the common mechanism.

hlg_8cc6881ea295c041_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable authorized group representatives to submit purchase orders while ensuring their identity is verified before submission.
hlg_8cc6881ea295c041_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the purchasing group representative to submit orders using unique credentials or group ID, establishing the authorization mechanism. llg_002 ensures that before submission, the system verifies the representative’s identity via two-factor authentication or group approval workflow, adding a mandatory verification step. Together, they define a secure, identity-verified order submission process for authorized group representatives.

hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to monitor, manage, and resolve wallet balance issues for order transactions through real-time notifications, grace periods, multiple recharge methods, and automated order cancellation if insufficient funds persist.
hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to check wallet balance and payment status, establishing visibility into funds. llg_002 provides real-time payment notifications to inform customers of transaction status. llg_003 introduces a grace period for insufficient balance, allowing customers time to top up before cancellation. llg_004 and llg_005 provide two distinct recharge methods (in-store terminal and online transfer) to replenish funds. llg_006 triggers an email warning at order placement if funds are insufficient, ensuring early alert. llg_007 triggers an SMS reminder before Monday evening to prompt timely action. llg_008 automatically cancels orders if funds remain insufficient after Monday evening, enforcing financial accountability. Together, these LLGs form a complete lifecycle for managing wallet funds during order transactions, including proactive alerts, multiple recharge options, and automated cancellation as a last resort.

hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to monitor, manage, and resolve wallet balance issues for order transactions through real-time notifications, grace periods, multiple recharge methods, and automated order cancellation if insufficient funds persist.
hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to check wallet balance and payment status, establishing visibility into funds. llg_002 provides real-time payment notifications to inform customers of transaction status. llg_003 introduces a grace period for insufficient balance, allowing customers time to top up before cancellation. llg_004 and llg_005 provide two distinct recharge methods (in-store terminal and online transfer) to replenish funds. llg_006 triggers an email warning at order placement if funds are insufficient, ensuring early alert. llg_007 triggers an SMS reminder before Monday evening to prompt timely action. llg_008 automatically cancels orders if funds remain insufficient after Monday evening, enforcing financial accountability. Together, these LLGs form a complete lifecycle for managing wallet funds during order transactions, including proactive alerts, multiple recharge options, and automated cancellation as a last resort.

hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to monitor, manage, and resolve wallet balance issues for order transactions through real-time notifications, grace periods, multiple recharge methods, and automated order cancellation if insufficient funds persist.
hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to check wallet balance and payment status, establishing visibility into funds. llg_002 provides real-time payment notifications to inform customers of transaction status. llg_003 introduces a grace period for insufficient balance, allowing customers time to top up before cancellation. llg_004 and llg_005 provide two distinct recharge methods (in-store terminal and online transfer) to replenish funds. llg_006 triggers an email warning at order placement if funds are insufficient, ensuring early alert. llg_007 triggers an SMS reminder before Monday evening to prompt timely action. llg_008 automatically cancels orders if funds remain insufficient after Monday evening, enforcing financial accountability. Together, these LLGs form a complete lifecycle for managing wallet funds during order transactions, including proactive alerts, multiple recharge options, and automated cancellation as a last resort.

hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to browse farmer offers, compare products, place orders with minimum quantity constraints, modify orders due to availability issues using precedence and fair-play rules, review and accept modified orders, and cancel orders when all products are unavailable with notification.
hlg_5f093c1983a0bd77_001.rationale: llg_001 enables viewing product origin details including certifications and availability; llg_002 enables browsing and comparing farmer offers by price, quantity, and characteristics; llg_003 enables placing orders with minimum quantity constraints; llg_004 enables modifying orders due to availability constraints using precedence rules and fair-play score; llg_005 enables reviewing and accepting modified orders; llg_006 enables automatic cancellation of orders when all products are unavailable with customer notification.

hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to monitor, manage, and resolve wallet balance issues for order transactions through real-time notifications, grace periods, multiple recharge methods, and automated order cancellation if insufficient funds persist.
hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to check wallet balance and payment status, establishing visibility into funds. llg_002 provides real-time payment notifications to inform customers of transaction status. llg_003 introduces a grace period for insufficient balance, allowing customers time to top up before cancellation. llg_004 and llg_005 provide two distinct recharge methods (in-store terminal and online transfer) to replenish funds. llg_006 triggers an email warning at order placement if funds are insufficient, ensuring early alert. llg_007 triggers an SMS reminder before Monday evening to prompt timely action. llg_008 automatically cancels orders if funds remain insufficient after Monday evening, enforcing financial accountability. Together, these LLGs form a complete lifecycle for managing wallet funds during order transactions, including proactive alerts, multiple recharge options, and automated cancellation as a last resort.

hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customer pickup scheduling with automated reminders, forfeiture handling, and fair-play score updates based on pickup compliance.
hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customer selection of pickup time slots based on store availability; llg_002 provides pre-pickup notifications to confirm attendance; llg_003 notifies customers of missed pickups and informs them of forfeit policy consequences; llg_004 automatically marks uncollected orders as forfeited by Friday and triggers score updates; llg_005 updates the customer’s fair-play score based on forfeited or missed pickups, affecting future order precedence. Together, these LLGs form a complete lifecycle for pickup management including scheduling, notification, forfeiture, and scoring.

hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable dynamic, rule-governed allocation of limited product quantities between competing customer orders based on real-time availability estimates and fair-play precedence scoring, with farmer confirmation of final quantities.
hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.rationale: llg_001 introduces the capability for a farmer to submit an availability estimate that triggers dynamic allocation between Friday noon and Saturday morning. llg_002 adds the requirement for the farmer to confirm final quantities by Monday morning, which adjusts order fulfillment. llg_003 introduces the system’s automatic application of precedence rules based on fair-play scores to allocate limited quantities when insufficient availability exists — this is a distinct, rule-based allocation mechanism that must be explicitly included to avoid masking its unique scope. Together, these LLGs define a system that combines real-time availability input, farmer confirmation, and rule-based allocation under scarcity — no generalized or inferred functionality is added.

hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.rationale: llg_001 enables store employees to view and manage pending orders for fulfillment; llg_002 adds the capability to coordinate pickup logistics including time and location; llg_003 introduces payment processing and wallet balance updates via system API; llg_004 adds the capability to confirm delivery status and update system records. Together, these cover the full lifecycle of order fulfillment from initiation to delivery confirmation, with explicit handling of pickup logistics and payment integration.

The current low-level goals (LLGs) are complete and correctly realize the parent high-level goal (HLG). The LLGs cover both the authorization of group representatives to submit orders and the verification of their identity. The system uses unique credentials or a group ID for authorization, and it validates the representative's identity through group membership validation and credential authentication. Customers are representatives of purchasing groups, such as families or groups of people, and only the registered representative of each group can submit an order.' The system checks that the quantities selected respect the minimum order constraints before confirming the order, ensuring accountability and integrity in the group-based purchasing process.

There are no unsupported or misleading LLGs. Each LLG has a clear, documented function related to the parent HLG: enabling only registered representatives of purchasing groups to submit orders while verifying their identity.

hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customers to monitor, manage, and resolve wallet balance issues for order transactions through real-time notifications, grace periods, multiple recharge methods, and automated order cancellation if insufficient funds persist.
hlg_1c190ea7f86685cf_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customers to check wallet balance and payment status, establishing visibility into funds. llg_002 provides real-time payment notifications to inform customers of transaction status. llg_003 introduces a grace period for insufficient balance, allowing customers time to top up before cancellation. llg_004 and llg_005 provide two distinct recharge methods (in-store terminal and online transfer) to replenish funds. llg_006 triggers an email warning at order placement if funds are insufficient, ensuring early alert. llg_007 triggers an SMS reminder before Monday evening to prompt timely action. llg_008 automatically cancels orders if funds remain insufficient after Monday evening, enforcing financial accountability. Together, these LLGs form a complete lifecycle for managing wallet funds during order transactions, including proactive alerts, multiple recharge options, and automated cancellation as a last resort.

Handle insufficient balance with grace period

hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable customer pickup scheduling with automated reminders, forfeiture handling, and fair-play score updates based on pickup compliance.
hlg_45d7b64c9eb54357_001.rationale: llg_001 enables customer selection of pickup time slots based on store availability; llg_002 provides pre-pickup notifications to confirm attendance; llg_003 notifies customers of missed pickups and informs them of forfeit policy consequences; llg_004 automatically marks uncollected orders as forfeited by Friday and triggers score updates; llg_005 updates the customer’s fair-play score based on forfeited or missed pickups, affecting future order precedence. Together, these LLGs form a complete lifecycle for pickup management including scheduling, notification, forfeiture, and scoring.

hlg_d7aace6841b88a6b_001.rationale: llg_001 introduces the capability for a farmer to submit an availability estimate that triggers dynamic allocation between Friday noon and Saturday morning. llg_002 adds the requirement for the farmer to confirm final quantities by Monday morning, which adjusts order fulfillment. llg_003 introduces the system’s automatic application of precedence rules based on fair-play scores to allocate limited quantities when insufficient availability exists — this is a distinct, rule-based allocation mechanism that must be explicitly included to avoid masking its unique scope. hlg_d714bbf6da86e761_001.rationale: llg_001 enables store employees to view and manage pending orders for fulfillment; llg_002 adds the capability to coordinate pickup logistics including time and location; llg_003 introduces payment processing and wallet balance updates via system API; llg_004 adds the capability to confirm delivery status and update system records. hlg_c12fcb1e0bd72453_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a delivery delay notification and compensation system that alerts farmers and customers via SMS, updates order records with status and reason, and automatically credits back missing amounts with a 20% bonus when delivery fails by 8 p.m. on Tuesday.
